purpose: Check whether every Grade 1-6 taxonomy concept resolves to at least one misconception and at least one diagnostic question after all registered diagnostic extensions are applied.
method: Load all 121 concept profiles from the concept intelligence manifest.
Load base misconception and diagnostic-question catalogs.
Apply every registered diagnostic link to the matching concept profile and deduplicate IDs.
Count a concept as diagnostic-route covered only when the resolved profile has at least one misconception ID and at least one diagnostic-question ID.

final_gap_closed.focus: Place-value unit exchange during regrouping rather than digit-level borrowing rules.

quality_cautions: Coverage is structural and instructional, not psychometric validation.
A diagnostic question is a probe for follow-up discussion; one response must not be used as a definitive diagnosis.
Some misconception records are curriculum-inferred and should be strengthened with misconception-specific research where available.
Language demand must be considered separately from mathematical understanding in bilingual classrooms.
Curriculum placement evidence and diagnostic evidence are separate layers; a strong curriculum source does not automatically validate a misconception claim.
interpretation_rule: Use the Elicit → Probe → Classify → Respond → Recheck process from diagnostic_interpretation_rules.json before presenting a likely misconception to a teacher.
